justification: Static analysis reveals high average fan-out (3.95) and tight cross-module coupling, especially in services/ (e.g., services/subscription.py imports 14+ modules, services/common.py and services/tasks.py directly call services.cloudflare.register, services.account calls services.cloudflare.updatePublicKey — creating circular-like dependencies). The repository tree shows modules importing from each other without clear dependency direction, violating module boundaries. This coupling increases ripple effects during change and degrades testability (e.g., tests/test_utils.py is the only test and only covers utils, not services/models). Implementing reduced coupling will isolate modules, allowing independent evolution and testing.
expected_architectural_change: Introduce abstractions (e.g., AccountRepository, EntrypointProvider, CloudflareService) to break direct inter-service dependencies. Services will depend on interfaces instead of concrete implementations, flattening the imports graph. Modules like services/cloudflare.py and services/common.py will no longer import each other, and shared data (e.g., Account, Entrypoint) will be passed via well-defined contracts instead of direct access.
implementation_strategy: Step 1: Extract interfaces for shared behaviors (e.g., CloudflareClient interface in services/, used by services/account.py and services/common.py). Step 2: Use dependency injection (e.g., via factory or minimal DI container) instead of direct imports in services/cloudflare.py → services/common.py. Step 3: Move common utilities used across services into shared interfaces or domain abstractions (e.g., EntrypointAggregator for utils/entrypoints.py). Step 4: Refactor services/cloudflare.py to be the only module importing models.Account directly; other services receive Account objects as arguments or via service methods.
risks: Initial refactoring may increase complexity due to new interfaces; risk of over-engineering if abstraction layers are premature. However, given the clear modular structure (e.g., services/, models/, utils/ directories) and current monolithic coupling, incremental application (starting with high-fan-out modules like services/subscription.py and services/tasks.py) mitigates this. Testing coverage must be preserved by adding tests for new abstractions.
